1. Exemption allowed subject to just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.

CM APPL. 36570/2025 (Stay)
3.

This is an application filed on behalf of the applicant/petitioner under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 seeking ad-interim ex-parte stay of the notice dated 03.06.2025 bearing Notification No. AD/LAC/SW/2025-26/42715 with Subject: "Sub:- Joint programmer for demolition and handing over of Awarded Land of Khasra No. 10/5/2 (2- 04), 6/1 (1-14), 12/11 (4-06), 12/2 (1-09), 19 (4-16), 20/1 (0-07), 22 (4-16), 23/1 (1-12) and 27 (0-10)
vide Award No. 30/2002-03/SW of Village Pochanpur scheduled on 09/06/2025 at 11:00 AM."
And the Notification This is a digitally signed order.

4.

Ms. Sumitra Chaudhary, learned counsel appearing for the applicant/petitioner submits that the impugned notice dated 03.06.2025 has been passed unilaterally by the respondent without even conducting the survey as directed by this Court vide order dated 17.12.2024.

She also submits that,
that apart the respondents LAC as also the GNCTD have failed to file the counter affidavit as directed vide the same order.
5. He submits that the duration of six days which have been given according to the impugned notice dated 03.06.2025 for a proposed demolition of 09.06.2025 is less than 15 days as provided by the Supreme Court in Contempt Petition No. 335/2021 titled as Sultana Shaheen vs. Durga Shankar Mishra & Anr.

entities.text: Sultana Shaheen vs. Durga Shankar Mishra & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She submits that thus the respondents cannot carry out the proposed demolition and this Court may restrain the respondents from doing so.

6. Mr. Pathak, learned counsel appearing for the LAC and Mr. Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the DDA submits that insofar as the subject lands are concerned, it is only for those portions which are specifically pointed out in the notice dated 03.06.2025, in which such action will be taken.

He also refers to the judgment of the Supreme Court in Delhi Development Authority v. Tejpal and Ors.,(2024) 7 SCC 433 to submit that since the subject land of the said particular notification falls in List - E.2, and the direction of the Supreme Court is clear that the authorities are required to take over the lands for the project development and if at all, the This is a digitally signed order.

7. In order to appreciate the contentions raised by learned counsel for parties, it would be relevant to note para 8 of the order dated 17.12.2025 passed by this Court while issuing notice in the present writ petition which reads as under:-
"8.
The Supreme Court, finally, vide judgment dated 17th May, 2024 titled Delhi Development Authority v. Tejpal and Ors.,(2024 INSC 456), disposed of all the said appeals filed by the DDA.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority v. Tejpal and Ors.,(2024 INSC 456)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Supreme Court drew up various lists and categorised the parties and gave separate directions in respect of the said parties.

The operative portion of the said Supreme Court decision in para 66 is set out below:-
"66.
All such civil appeals are accordingly allowed, the impugned judgment of the High Court in each case is set aside, and the acquisition of the respondents' lands under 1894 Act is consequently upheld.

This will, however, not preclude the Attar Singh & Anr vs Delhi Development Authority & Ors on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26922867/
2 respondents from recovery of the compensation amount, if not already paid or to the extent it is not paid, along with interest and other statutory benefits under 1894 Act.

entities.text: Attar Singh & Anr vs Delhi Development Authority & Ors on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, they shall be at liberty to seek reference under Section 18 of the 1894 Act in accordance with law.

The Government of NCT of Delhi and its authorities are directed to take physical possession of the lands falling under this category (i.e., 'List- E.2'), if not already taken and continue uninterruptedly to complete the public infrastructure projects."
8.
It is not disputed that the lands which are subject matter of the notice dated 03.06.2025 fall within List-E.2 as observed by the Supreme Court in Tejpal (supra).

There cannot be any ambiguity in understanding the directions passed by the Supreme Court.
9.

What we find from the order passed in Tejpal (supra), particularly in para 66 which has been extracted in para 8 of the order dated 17.12.2024 of this Court is that there has been a direction and a mandate upon the Government of NCT, Delhi and other authorities to take physical possession of the lands falling under the category List-E.2, if not already undertaken, and for such possession to continue uninterruptedly to
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/06/2025 at 12:14:31 complete the public infrastructure projects.

10. In that view of the matter and the fact that the Supreme Court has already rendered its opinion on the subject lands which form part of the Notification dated 03.06.2025, this Court is not going to interfere or interdict any such measure being undertaken by the respondent in compliance of the Supreme Court order in Tejpal (supra).
11.
In that view of the matter, we do not find any merit in the present application.
The same is dismissed.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J (VACATION JUDGE) HARISH VAIDYANATHAN SHANKAR, J (VACATION JUDGE) JUNE 6, 2025/neha
